posts.title: A 27-byte telemetry response nobody reads freezes Claude Desktop every two days
posts.description: TL;DR: Claude Desktop on Linux froze dead every couple of days, with empty logs. It took two months and a 1.5 TiB core dump to find out why. The app never reads a 27-byte telemetry reply, and Chromium keeps a file descriptor open for each one until the renderer runs out of them. Chromium says it works as intended, and Anthropic's bot closed my issue as "not about Claude Code".

posts.title: fsync gives you durability and ordering, but often you only need ordering
posts.description: TL;DR: fsync promises two things, durability and ordering, and I only need ordering. ext4 gives both or neither: every fsync commits the journal and flushes the disk cache. ZFS with sync=disabled gives ordering alone: transaction groups land in order, and a crash loses the last tens of seconds, not a database. My two HDDs are 2.7% busy instead of 13%, and a write takes 2 ms instead of 16.

posts.title: Wanted to download an ISO, ended up writing a kernel exploit
posts.description: TL;DR: My TP-Link EAP770 v1 corrupts downloads over Wi-Fi and TP-Link EOL'd it before I unboxed it. The fix is two zeros in sysfs. TP-Link's shell won't let me write them, so I wrote a kernel exploit for my own fucking access point.
